The heirs of the recorded owners Momena Khatun, Shah Ahmed Chowdhury and others, the predecessors of the petitioners filed an objection under diary No. 4131 dated 27th July, 1981, against the said application stating amongst others that the property sought to he enrolled is their personal property and not Waqf property of Jinnat Ali Waqf state. Earlier on 30th December, 1977, late Moulvi Muhammad Harun filed an application for enrolment and misc. E.C. No. 15 of 1979 was started and objection was filed by Moulavi Shah Ahmed Chowdhury and others stating that the property of Waqf of Jinnat Ali had already enrolled as Waqf property in E.C. No. 4401, and the Mutwalli is not coming forward for enrolment of the disputed property as Waqf property because Jinnat Ali had no interest in it, but the enrolment was not made since file of EC. No. 4401 was called for by Ministry of LA and L.R., Govt. of Bangladesh.  5. Against the said order dated 2nd April, 1986, the petitioners filed an application under section 50 read with section 35 of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962, before the learned District Judge, Chittagong which was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 173 of 1986. The respondent No. 1 filed written objection against the said application stating amongst other that the property is Waqf property of Jinnat Ali Waqf Estate and earlier it was excluded simply on assumption. 

 6. In the said Miscellaneous Case the above Respondent filed an application for hearing the issue of maintainability to which the petitioners objected. Thereafter in the Miscellaneous Case, the Respondent filed an application under order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejecting it stating that the case is barred by law. The petitioners filed objection stating that order 7 Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure cannot be applied in a proceeding under Waqf Ordinance. 

 7. The Additional District Judge by judgment and order dated 8th May, 2006, allowed the prayer and rejected the Miscellaneous Case, against which, the petitioners filed F.M.A. No. 151 of 2006 before the High Court Division, which was heard by a Single Bench. The learned Judge after hearing allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and order of the teamed Additional District Judge passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 173 of 1986. In the judgment the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division made observations that the property in question shall continue as Waqf property, against which, the petitioners filed C.P.No. 60 of 2008 before this Division. Respondent No. 1 also filed C.P.No. 214 of 2008 against the judgment and order of the High Court Division. Both the petitions were heard one after another and by the impugned judgment and order dated 24th March, 2009, both of them were dismissed. 

 8. It is contended by Mr. Rokanuddin Mahmud that the petitioners did not challenge the judgment and order of the High Court Division on merit, they in fact, filed the leave petition for expunging the observations made in the judgment that "It does not however mean that the waqf nature of the property shall be in any way changed or disturbed, the property which was made waqf on 3.8.1867 shall continue as waqf property"……. the property in question shall continue as waqf property". It is argued that if such observations remain in the judgment, the petitioners will he prejudiced, inasmuch as, they will be deprived of showing that the property is not waqf property at the hearing of the main case before the learned Additional District Judge. Mr. Rokanuddin Mahmud, in the premises, argues that he is no inclined to press this petition on merit and this petition may he dismissed for ends of justice keeping the issue in dispute open with certain observations so that the petitioners will be able to raise the matter on merit in the court below. 

 9. In view of the submissions of the learned Counsel, this review petition is dismissed with the observation that whatever findings and observations made by the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 151 of 2006 will not be binding upon the Additional District Judge in the disposal of Miscellaneous Case No. 173 of 1986, and that the learned Additional District Judge will be at liberty to dispose of the said case on merit.
